key_insight: A human-centered audit shows that different Shapley-value variants—though theoretically similar—diverge in semantics and practical utility, and common quantitative proxies often fail to predict which explanations help humans in high-stakes, low-latency settings.
problem_solved: Clarifies which Shapley formulations actually align with human decision-making and operational constraints, addressing the gap between theoretical metrics and real-world usefulness of explanations.
method: Develop a unified amortized framework to isolate semantic differences between eight Shapley variants under low-latency operational constraints.
Compare variants using both quantitative proxies and human-centered evaluations (audits) in high-stakes decision tasks to measure alignment with human utility.
Analyze discrepancies between proxy-based rankings and human performance/preferences to identify failure modes and practical trade-offs.
impact: Provides practitioners with empirical guidance on selecting and interpreting Shapley-based explanations under time-sensitive, high-risk conditions, and motivates integrating human-centered benchmarks into XAI evaluation pipelines.
visual_elements: Framework diagram: unified amortized pipeline showing how different Shapley variants are generated and evaluated under latency constraints.
Bar/heatmap: comparison of 8 Shapley variants showing alignment with quantitative proxies vs. human utility (highlighting mismatches).
Trade-off infographic: latency vs. fidelity vs. human usefulness with icons for operational constraints and high-stakes decisions.
Decision-flow vignette: a short storyboard showing how explanations influence a human decision in a high-stakes scenario.
paper_title: Rethinking XAI Evaluation: A Human-Centered Audit of Shapley Benchmarks in High-Stakes Settings
paper_authors: Inês Oliveira e Silva, Sérgio Jesus, Iker Perez, Rita P. Ribeiro, Carlos Soares
